title: Local Confluence Conditions

basis.scope: Canonical local confluence conditions for divergent lawful reductions from a common origin, including branch objects, joinability, critical pair classification, and the explicit distinction from global confluence and termination.

core_rule.statement: Local confluence is a bounded property of lawful reduction branches from a common origin; joinability compares process-equivalent branch outcomes under the current reduction system; critical pairs are the immediate divergent branch pairs evaluated by the local condition; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the necessary and sufficient local conditions under which divergent lawful reductions may be considered locally confluent without asserting global confluence.

canonical_claims.statement: Local confluence is a bounded reduction property over lawful branches from a common origin.
Joinability is the branch-level condition used to compare process-equivalent continuation outcomes.
Critical pairs are the immediate divergent lawful reductions used for local confluence evaluation.
Local confluence does not imply global confluence or termination.

formal_objects.name: Local Confluence
formal_objects.definition: A property stating that two lawful reductions diverging from the same continuation may be reduced to equivalent continuation outcomes under the current reduction system.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Branch
formal_objects.definition: A lawful reduction path originating from a common continuation expression.

formal_objects.name: Joinability
formal_objects.definition: A relation indicating that two lawful reduction branches can be reduced to process-equivalent continuation outcomes.

formal_objects.name: Critical Reduction Pair
formal_objects.definition: A pair of immediately divergent lawful reductions originating from the same continuation requiring local confluence evaluation.

canonical_conditions.description: Both branches originate from the same continuation expression.
Each branch satisfies WF(C), typing, admissibility, residue propagation, and evaluation order.
Each branch independently satisfies all reduction requirements.
Both branches may be reduced to equivalent continuation outcomes.
Equivalent NF(C), pNF(C), or identical classified ⊥C_x outcomes are preserved.

branch_rules: Each branch must preserve process equivalence.
Branches may differ in intermediate reductions.
Branch ordering is not required to be identical.
Trace equivalence remains independent of branch identity.
Joinability is evaluated after lawful reduction.
invariants: Local confluence does not imply global confluence.
Joinability does not imply identical traces.
